The Death Penalty is more expensive than life in prison.

The average cost per year for a prisoner is anywhere from $20,000 to $40,000 per year, depending on location. James Holmes is currently 27, so if he lives to be 70, it will cost taxpayers between $860,000 and $1,720,000, without including any extra costs for unforseen medical fees etc and this is after court fees. The execution drugs themselves can cost as little as $83. Often times people add in court fees and incarceration fees, but those are mostly already present. Considering this is a pretty open and shut case, long drawn out court battles wont happen, and appeals would be fairly quick if granted. In this particular case it will likely be cheaper to execute him than to give him life in prison. Most of the extra costs associated come from appeals of cases that aren't so obvious where a lot of extra research is involved.
